metadata.title: RFK Jr. is investigating whether troops died of Covid vaccine, Army doctor says

sources.news_title: Theresa Long is reviewing 2,544 unverified death reports and military databases as Pentagon analyses found no vaccine-related deaths.
sources.text:
Authored by AG News Staff via American Greatness,
The Trump administration is investigating whether COVID-19 vaccines contributed to the deaths of U.S. service members following the Biden administration’s military vaccine mandate, according to testimony from an Army doctor assigned to the effort.
Army physician Theresa Long said in an Aug. 14 federal court deposition that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth detailed her to serve as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s senior medical military adviser.
Long said she is examining 2,544 unverified reports of deaths among service members submitted to the federal Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, or VAERS, following COVID vaccination.
VAERS is an early-warning surveillance system that accepts reports of health problems occurring after vaccination. A report does not establish that a vaccine caused the medical event or death.
Long, who is board certified in aerospace medicine and holds a master’s degree in public health, said she hopes to complete her investigation within a year.
She also testified that she knows of 28 people who died because of COVID vaccines but said she was not permitted to provide additional information supporting that assertion.
The investigation comes as the Trump administration reexamines the military’s handling of the COVID pandemic and the Biden administration’s 2021 vaccine mandate.
Nearly 9,000 service members were discharged for refusing COVID vaccinations before Congress ordered the Pentagon to rescind the mandate in 2022. The Defense Department has since established a COVID-19 Reinstatement and Reconciliation Task Force to assist troops who left the military over the requirement and want to return.
“The Department continues to right the wrongs of the past and to restore confidence in, and honor to, our fighting force,” the Pentagon said in announcing the task force.
Long is also reviewing military health surveillance systems and two medical databases from the pandemic period.
A 2026 Pentagon report found an increase in myocarditis and pericarditis among active-duty service members shortly after COVID vaccination, but said the increase was not sustained over one year. The report did not identify vaccine-related deaths.
The FDA has also required updated warnings for mRNA COVID vaccines concerning myocarditis and pericarditis. The agency reported a higher incidence among young men, with 27 cases per million vaccinations compared with 8 per million in the general population for the period it analyzed.
Long’s previously undisclosed assignment indicates that the Trump administration’s review of the Biden-era military vaccine mandate now extends beyond reinstating discharged troops to examining whether the vaccines themselves caused serious injuries or deaths among service members.

Army physician Dr. Theresa Long said she is working with the Trump administration to investigate whether 2,544 unverified deaths reported among U.S. service members in the federal vaccine adverse-event database were connected to COVID-19 vaccination, with the review expected to take up to a year.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
An Army physician working with the Trump administration is examining whether thousands of deaths reported among U.S. service members to the federal Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System were connected to COVID-19 vaccines administered under the military’s former mandate.
Dr. Theresa Long said in an Aug. 14 federal court deposition that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth selected her to serve as a senior medical military adviser to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., according to Politico.
Long said she is investigating 2,544 unverified deaths involving service members that were reported to HHS’ Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, or VAERS, to determine whether any were caused by or otherwise connected to COVID-19 vaccination.
VAERS reports alone do not establish that a vaccine caused an injury or death. The system accepts reports of health events occurring after vaccination, including events that may ultimately prove unrelated, meaning the cases require further investigation before causation can be determined.
Long told the court that she hopes to complete her research into potential vaccine-related health complications “within a year,” according to Politico.
Neither the Pentagon nor HHS has publicly announced conclusions from the investigation.
The Pentagon referred the Daily Caller News Foundation to HHS when asked for comment, while HHS did not immediately respond. Long also could not immediately be reached.
The Department of War separately told Politico that it does not “have anything to announce at this time” concerning Long’s reported role as Kennedy’s senior medical military adviser.
The department instead referred the outlet to a May 8 statement addressing military personnel affected by the previous COVID-19 vaccination policy.
The Pentagon “continues to take decisive action in support of the many Service members adversely impacted by the COVID-19 vaccine mandate,” the statement said in part.
The investigation fits within a broader Trump administration reassessment of vaccine mandates and policies imposed on military personnel during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
Kennedy has repeatedly criticized aspects of federal vaccine policy and has pledged to eliminate COVID-19 vaccination mandates.
In an August 2026 post, Kennedy pledged to “end covid vaccine mandates” in the United States.
He has also said that rebuilding public confidence in federal vaccine policy requires greater transparency.
In an August 2025 post, Kennedy said his “job” as health secretary is to “restore trust in the vaccine program so that parents know we’re telling them the truth.”
Hegseth has similarly criticized mandatory vaccination policies within the military.
In June, he called the military’s flu-vaccine requirement an “absurd, overreaching mandate,” according to NPR.
The Trump administration had already begun reversing Biden-era military COVID-19 policies shortly after President Donald Trump returned to office.
In January 2025, Trump issued an executive order directing the reinstatement of service members who had been discharged for refusing the military’s COVID-19 vaccine requirement.
The order recounted the history of the mandate and sharply criticized its implementation.
“On August 24, 2021, the Secretary of Defense mandated that all service members receive the COVID-19 vaccine,” according to the order. “The Secretary of Defense later rescinded the mandate on January 10, 2023. The vaccine mandate was an unfair, overbroad and completely unnecessary burden on our service members. Further, the military unjustly discharged those who refused the vaccine, regardless of the years of service given to our Nation, after failing to grant many of them an exemption that they should have received.”
The military vaccination requirement began under the Biden administration in August 2021 and remained in effect until January 2023.
Service members who refused vaccination could face administrative or disciplinary consequences, including separation from the military, although policies varied by service branch and individual circumstances.
The Trump administration has since moved to restore personnel removed under those policies while reviewing broader questions surrounding the mandate’s consequences.
Long’s inquiry now adds a medical component to that reassessment by examining whether deaths and other reported adverse events among troops can be scientifically linked to COVID-19 vaccination.
Her investigation does not establish that the 2,544 reported deaths were caused by vaccines.
Rather, the cases represent unverified reports submitted to VAERS that Long said she intends to analyze for evidence of a causal relationship.
The distinction will be central to any final conclusions because VAERS is designed as an early-warning surveillance system rather than a database of confirmed vaccine injuries.
Long’s stated one-year timetable suggests the administration’s review could continue into 2027 as federal officials examine medical records, timing, diagnoses and other factors necessary to determine whether particular health outcomes were caused by vaccination or occurred coincidentally afterward.

U.S. Army doctor claims 28 troops died from Covid vaccines | 4 Sep 2026 | A U.S. Army doctor has testified that she knows of 28 U.S. military deaths caused by Covid-19 vaccines, Politico has reported citing a court deposition. The U.S. government is investigating 2,544 deaths reported following the jabs, the official has said. Theresa Long, who also serves as an adviser to U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., reportedly gave the testimony during an August 14 deposition in a federal court case in Virginia. Neither her testimony nor her role at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) had previously been reported. Long allegedly said that the 2,544 unverified deaths were reported to the department’s Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS). Former U.S. President [sic] Joe Biden ordered all US military staff to be vaccinated or be discharged from service, resulting in over 9,000 dismissals. After returning to office, President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to offer reinstatement to those who had been discharged for refusing a vaccine.

The Department of Health and Human Services has hired an Army doctor with a history of questioning the safety of COVID vaccines to investigate unsubstantiated claims that more than 2,500 U.S. service members died after receiving the shots.
The hiring of Lt. Col. Theresa Long, who has no specialized training in vaccines or viruses, is part of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s campaign to explore baseless theories about the hazards of vaccines.
There is little evidence to support this latest investigation. More than 96% of service members were vaccinated against COVID before a mandate that they receive the shots was rescinded. A March report from the Pentagon, and one in July 2025, found no deaths from the vaccines.
Long said in an Aug. 14 legal deposition obtained by The New York Times that she is a senior medical military adviser to Kennedy but also reports to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
She said in the deposition that she had been appointed to investigate 55,000 reports of adverse effects and 2,544 deaths among service members who received COVID vaccines, in the federal Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System. Experts have noted that while this database is the largest, it is also the least reliable: Reports of side effects can be submitted by anyone and are not vetted.
Long and HHS did not respond to requests for comment.
Billions worldwide have received COVID vaccines. The vast majority have experienced no serious side effects.
Long testified that she had personal knowledge of the deaths of 28 service members as a result of COVID vaccines. She also said that she knew of several service members who lost pregnancies after receiving COVID shots, and that the vaccines had caused pregnancy loss at a rate of about 82%. Studies in hundreds of thousands of women have shown that COVID vaccination is not linked to an increased risk of miscarriage, stillbirth or preterm birth.
The 2026 Pentagon report concluded that COVID vaccinations caused a short-term rise in heart inflammation within 21 days -- a known side effect -- but that the inflammation did not persist, and COVID Itself carried a larger risk of the complication.
Long told lawyers in the deposition that the Pentagon report cherry-picked data and that she had been appointed specifically to investigate “inaccuracies” in defense databases. She said she hoped to complete her investigation within a year.
This article originally appeared in The New York Times.
